title: Microsoft Fabric for Microsoft 365 Admins: What You Need to Know
description:
Microsoft Fabric often appears in a tenant before anyone has planned its governance. This episode gives Microsoft 365 admins the platform view: how capacities, OneLake, workspaces, tenant settings, identity, labels and licensing fit together. It ends with a practical 30-day plan to put owners and guardrails in place before data and costs drift.
In this episode
00:00 – Why Fabric lands on the M365 admin's desk06:36 – Capacities, throttling and monitoring18:57 – OneLake: one copy for the tenant22:09 – Workspaces, items and tenant settings38:11 – Identity and the layered security model57:09 – Connecting Microsoft 365 data, Copilot and auditing75:39 – A 30-day admin plan and common failures
Key takeaways
Fabric runs as one shared platform inside your tenant, so a single capacity is at once a billing object, a performance boundary and a blast radius.Workspaces are the real unit of control, so every workspace needs a name, an owner, group-based roles and a lifecycle before sprawl sets in.Security, labels and AI agents only protect what is configured at every layer, so review tenant settings, OneLake access paths and copied Microsoft 365 data early.
Worth quoting
“A capacity unit isn't a server or a machine. It's a measure of how much work the platform can do for you per second, and every action in fabric costs some amount of it.” – Mirko Peters (06:56)
“You stop controlling data by controlling where it lives. You start controlling it by controlling who can reach it.” – Mirko Peters (20:56)
